title: Subsidiary books
examples: What is the difference between the sales book and the cash book?
When do I use a purchase book instead of a general journal?
How do I transfer entries from the cash book to the ledger?

explain.say: Today we learn about subsidiary books in accounting.

items: Sales Book: Records credit sales only.
Purchase Book: Records credit purchases only.
Cash Book: Records all cash receipts and payments.

explain.say: The sales book records goods sold on credit to customers.
The purchase book records goods bought on credit from suppliers.
The cash book records every single amount of money coming in or going out.

draw.text: Cash Book: Cash In and Out

explain.say: If you sell something and get cash immediately, you use the cash book.
A common mistake is recording credit sales in the cash book.

draw.text: Credit sales belong in Sales Book

faq.q: Do I use the cash book for everything?
faq.a: No, the cash book is only for actual cash transactions. You use the sales book for sales made on credit.
asks: Where do I record cash sales?
Is the cash book for all transactions?

faq.q: What is the main difference between the sales book and the purchase book?
faq.a: The sales book tracks money owed to you by customers. The purchase book tracks money you owe to suppliers.
asks: What is the purpose of the two books?
Do I use one book or two for credit?

faq.q: If I pay cash to a supplier, which book do I use?
faq.a: You must use the cash book for any payment made using actual money. This shows your cash going out.
asks: Does paying cash go in the purchase book?

faq.q: Do I need to use a general journal at all?
faq.a: Generally, you use subsidiary books first. The general journal is reserved for unusual or non-routine transactions.
asks: When is the general journal used?
Can I skip the general journal?

faq.q: What if I sell something and get cash later?
faq.a: If you get cash later, you record the initial sale in the sales book. Then, when you receive the cash, you record it in the cash book.
asks: How do I record delayed cash?
Does the sales book cover all stages?

facts: The sales book records transactions where goods are sold on credit.
The purchase book records transactions where goods are bought on credit.
The cash book records all cash receipts and cash payments.
These books are subsidiary because they record specific types of transactions.

quiz.say: A business sells goods worth two hundred dollars and receives cash immediately. Which book records this?
quiz.why: The cash book records all actual cash movements, including immediate sales.

wrong.0: The sales book is only for sales made on credit, not for immediate cash.
wrong.1: The purchase book deals only with buying goods on credit from suppliers.
wrong.2: The general journal is for unusual items, not routine cash sales.

quiz.say: A business buys supplies on credit from a supplier for one hundred dollars. Which book records this?
quiz.why: The purchase book is specifically designed to record all purchases made on credit.

wrong.0: The sales book tracks goods sold to customers, not goods bought from suppliers.
wrong.1: While possible, the purchase book is the correct specialized book to use here.
wrong.3: The cash book only records transactions involving actual cash payments.

quiz.say: If a business receives cash from a customer who bought goods last month, which book is used?
quiz.why: Even if the original sale was recorded elsewhere, the receipt of cash must be recorded in the cash book.

wrong.1: The sales book records the initial credit sale, not the later cash receipt.
wrong.2: The purchase book only records purchases, not customer payments.
wrong.3: This is a routine cash receipt, which has its own dedicated book.
